q: 1. Plywood is normally available ............
explain: Common commercial plywood used for general purposes typically starts at a thickness of 3 mm to 4 mm.

q: 2. Plywood is made from ............
explain: Plywood is manufactured by gluing together thin layers (veneers) of Teak timber in alternating grain directions.

q: 3. The chromium content in stainless steel is more than ...............
explain: A minimum of about 10.5% to 11% chromium is required to form a passive layer of chromium oxide that protects the steel from corrosion.

q: 4. Invar is a nickel steel with nickel content between ...............
explain: Invar (FeNi36) contains approximately 36% nickel. It is famous for having a uniquely low coefficient of thermal expansion.

q: 5. The steel which contains fissures and cavities manufactured by ...............
explain: The steel which contains fissures and cavities is manufactured by the cementation process

q: 6. Age of tree may be ascertained by ...............
explain: Each year, a tree adds a new layer of wood. Counting these annual rings on a cross-section of the trunk gives the age of the tree.

q: 7. A well seasoned timber may contain moisture up to ............
explain: Seasoning aims to reduce moisture to 10-12%, which is roughly the equilibrium moisture content for most environments.

q: 8. The moisture content in timber for formwork should not exceed ..........
explain: For formwork, timber should have a moisture content around 15% to prevent excessive swelling or shrinkage when in contact with wet concrete.

q: 9. Invar contains .........
explain: Invar is a nickel-iron alloy notable for its uniquely low coefficient of thermal expansion. It specifically contains 36% nickel and 64% iron.

q: 10. The thickness of five-ply sheet varies from .............
explain: Depending on the thickness of individual veneers, a 5-ply board typically falls within the range of 6 mm to 9 mm thickness.

q: 11. The thickness of lamin boards vary from .............
explain: Lamin boards are a type of blockboard where the core is made of thin strips of wood. Their standard thickness ranges between 12 mm and 25 mm.

q: 12. Which one of the following does not belong to exogenous trees .............
explain: Coconut is an endogenous tree. Teak, Shisham, and Sal are exogenous trees, which are the primary source of timber used in engineering.

q: 13. Cast iron contains carbon approximately .............
explain: Cast iron typically has a high carbon content, generally ranging from 2% to 4% (the book option 0.15-5.5% encompasses the standard range).

q: 14. Steel contains carbon approximately .............
explain: Steel is an alloy of iron and carbon, where the carbon content is usually between 0.05% and 1.75%.

q: 15. Wrought iron contains carbon about .............
explain: Wrought iron is the purest form of iron, containing very little carbon (usually less than 0.15%).

q: 16. The moisture content in well seasoned timber is ............
explain: Seasoning reduces moisture to 10-12%, which is roughly the level where wood reaches equilibrium with the atmospheric humidity.

q: 17. The timber whose thickness is less than 5 cm and the width exceeds 12 cm, is called ......
explain: The timber whose thickness is less than 5 cm and the width exceeds 12 cm is called a board.

q: 18. The most valuable timber may be obtained from ............
explain: Teak is considered the king of timbers due to its durability, workability, and high resistance to decay and termites.

q: 19. Stainless steel resists corrosion due to ............
explain: Chromium reacts with oxygen to form a thin, invisible protective layer of chromium oxide that prevents further oxidation (corrosion).

q: 20. The age of the tree can be judged from ............
explain: Dendrochronology uses the counting of annual rings to determine the age of an exogenous tree.

q: 21. Wrought iron contains carbon upto ............
explain: Wrought iron is the purest form of iron, containing a very low carbon content, typically less than 0.15%.

q: 22. Forge pig may be converted to wrought iron by ............
explain: Puddling is the specific metallurgical process used to convert pig iron into wrought iron by oxidizing impurities in a reverberatory furnace.

q: 23. PVC stands for ............
explain: PVC is a common thermoplastic polymer known as Polyvinyl Chloride, widely used for pipes and insulation.
